verdict.reasoning: Patient states hearing problems on the left side for about three weeks: "Just one side, just on my left side..." and "it's been a few weeks now. Um, been about three weeks or something."
Patient reports numbness of the face on the left side: "my face has been feeling a bit numb recently" and "Yeah, so again it's the left side... my jawline's just all feeling a bit numb round here."

She describes the numbness around the left ear and jawline and that it is present most of the time: "around my left ear, and kind of, along here. So like, my jawline's just all feeling a bit numb" and "it kind of, kind of, there quite often, so, all the time. So yeah, right now it feels..."

Patient notes intermittent tinnitus with dizziness: "I think, occasionally noticed a, ringing in my ear" and later "like I said, like the ringing um, occasionally and, when I get that I can sometimes feel a bit dizzy." The side is not explicitly stated but context is the left ear symptoms.

She denies all listed symptoms: otalgia/otorrhea ("No, nothing coming out"; "Uh, no, don't think so"), fever ("No, nothing like that"), limb weakness/numbness ("No, no, no, no, nothing like that"), dysphagia ("No"), dysarthria/speaking difficulty ("No, no"), visual problems ("No, that's all good"). Itch/pruritus is queried but unanswered, so not denied; however the rest are accurately denied.
Patient reports nasal polyps: "I've got kind of, been told I have polyps in my nose in the past" and refers to "my nose polyps."
She mentions a past episode of labyrinthitis: "I think they said, ages ago, I had something called, can't quite remember but, labyrinthitis, something like that, but again, nothing, nothing ongoing."

She uses an as-needed nasal spray with unknown name: "if my nose polyps are playing up I've got a spray" and "I only take the, spray for my nose when I need it" and "Do you remember the name of the spray, at all?" "Unfortunately I don't, sorry."
She reports taking Rennies as needed: "I take a Rennie's if I need to" and "sometimes take like Rennies, but I just get that from the chemist."
Allergy to latex is stated: "Do you have any , any allergies to any medication?" Patient: "Uh, no just Latex."
Family history: "My brother had, Neurofibromatosis, I think it is."

Occupation and impact: "I'm a jockey" and "because of all the kind of, these symptoms I've been getting... I've just had to do far less training. So, kind of beginning to, yeah, impacting work, um, a little bit now."
Living situation and pets: "Yeah, yeah. Um, I, uh, live with my partner." and later "No, no pets."

This is a clinical interpretation consistent with the history: unilateral left hearing loss, left facial numbness, intermittent tinnitus and dizziness for ~3 weeks are described, and suggesting peripheral facial neuropathy or otologic pathology is a reasonable direct clinical inference from those findings.

Doctor explicitly considers Bell's palsy and need for in‑person neuro exam and ear exam: "what you're, what you're describing might be something called Bell's Palsy" and "I would like a GP to assess you... do a... neurological examination... Have a look inside the ear, see if there's any... anything to see within the ear."

Stroke red flags (limb weakness, speech difficulty, visual loss, severe acute onset) are specifically denied; doctor says, "from what you've told me, this doesn't seem to be... anything that you're gonna die from" and does not raise stroke concern. Thus, no red-flag stroke features are reported.

Doctor plans same‑day face‑to‑face assessment for neuro exam and otoscopy: "I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today" and "part of the reason... is... we can do a... neurological examination... Have a look inside the ear."

Specific examination components (forehead involvement, detailed sensory exam, gait/balance, audiologic bedside screening) are not mentioned in the transcript; only a general "neurological examination" is referenced.
There is no discussion of corticosteroids, antivirals, treatment window, or herpes zoster in the transcript; only that Bell’s palsy might be the diagnosis and would be explained later.
The transcript does not mention ENT referral, MRI, or urgent imaging; such escalation steps are not discussed.

Doctor gives admin and scheduling instructions: "I'm gonna send a message to our admin team... book you in for a face-to-face appointment" and "you can ring the support team number... they'll slot you in..." and stresses it should be done today: "please make sure the appointment gets done today."
While the doctor offers reassurance, there is no explicit mention of strict return precautions or instructions about returning if new neurological symptoms develop.
